title: حِكَايَةُ التَّاجِرِ وَأَوْلَادِهِ
titleEn: The Merchant and His Sons, continued
part: Night 44 · The Merchant and His Sons, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 347–350 (Night 44, continuing directly from nights-43), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition's Middle Arabic forms and its occasional compositor's slips, is preserved unaltered; a few genuinely obscure or corrupt-looking forms are vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 44 follows Qūt al-Qulūb as she recognises the sick stranger as Ghānim, restores him, his mother and his sister with baths, clothes and good food, and brings Ghānim before the Caliph, who is charmed by the verses he recites in praise of the Caliph. Shahrazād is overtaken by morning. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الرَّابِعَةُ وَالْأَرْبَعُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-rābiʿatu wa-al-arbaʿūna
sentences.l: And-when was the-night the-fourth and-the-forty.
sentences.i: And when it was the forty-fourth night,
sentences.n: The night formula. The ordinal is built “the fourth and the forty”: the unit comes first, joined by wa- to the tens, and both words agree with الليلة in the nominative, as in Classical. We vocalise what is printed.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُأَنَّ قُوتَ الْقُلُوبِ لَمَّا قَالَتْ لَهُمَا لَا تَحْزَنَا
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna Qūta al-Qulūbi lammā qālat lahumā lā taḥzanā
sentences.l: She-said: It-reached-me, O-you the-king the-felicitous, that Qūt al-Qulūb, when she-said to-the-two-of-them: Not grieve-(dual)!
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that when Qūt al-Qulūb said to the two of them, “Grieve no more,”
sentences.n: The printed السعيدان is a single word: the vocative's السعيد run together with أنّ (“that”), a print slip. We keep the letters as printed, vocalised as السعيد + أنّ. This unit is an unfinished subordinate clause (“when she said … ”); its main verb follows in the next unit.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهَا أَمَرَتِ الْعَرِيفَ أَنْ يَأْخُذَ هُمَا إِلَى بَيْتِهِ وَيُخَلِّيَ زَوْجَتَهُ تُدْخِلَهُمَا الْحَمَّامَ وَتُلْبِسَهُمَا ثِيَابًا حَسَنَةً وَتَتَوَصَّي بِهِمَا وَتُكْرِمَهُمَا غَايَةَ الْإِكْرَامِ
sentences.tr: thumma innahā amarat al-ʿarīfa an yaʾkhudha humā ilā baytihi wa-yukhalliya zawjatahu tudkhilahumā al-ḥammāma wa-tulbisahumā thiyāban ḥasanatan wa-tatawaṣṣī bihimā wa-tukrimahumā ghāyata al-ikrāmi
sentences.l: Then that-she commanded the-overseer that he-take them-two to his-house and-leave his-wife she-bring-in-them-two the-bath and-clothe-them-two garments good and-take-charge of-them-two and-honour-them-two utmost the-honouring.
sentences.i: Then she commanded the overseer to take the two of them to his house, and to have his wife bring them into the bath, clothe them in fine garments, care for them and honour them to the utmost.
sentences.n: ياخذ هما is printed as two words; it is يأخذهما, “take them (two)”. The verb تتوصي is printed with a final yāʾ, for Classical تَتَوَصَّى (“commend, take care”); we point the letters as printed. ويخلي زوجته تدخلهما is loose Middle Arabic syntax: “and let his wife bring them in”, with no linking أن before the second verb.

sentences.t: وَأَعْطَتْهُ جُمْلَةً مِنَ الْمَالِ
sentences.tr: wa-aʿṭathu jumlatan mina al-māli
sentences.l: And-she-gave-him a-sum of the-money.
sentences.i: And she gave him a sum of money.
sentences.n: من المال: مِنْ here introduces the substance of the sum (“of money”); the final nūn of مِنْ is vowelled with fatḥa (مِنَ) before the article's lām.

sentences.t: وَفِي ثَانِي يَوْمٍ رَكِبَتْ قُوتُ الْقُلُوبِ وَذَهَبَتْ إِلَى بَيْتِ الْعَرِيفِ وَدَخَلَتْ عِنْدَ زَوْجَتِهِ فَقَامَتْ إِلَيْهَا وَقَبَّلَتْ يَدَيْهَا وَشَكَرَتْ إِحْسَانَهَا
sentences.tr: wa-fī thānī yawmin rakibat Qūtu al-Qulūbi wa-dhahabat ilā bayti al-ʿarīfi wa-dakhalat ʿinda zawjatihi fa-qāmat ilayhā wa-qabbalat yadayhā wa-shakarat iḥsānahā
sentences.l: And-in second day rode Qūt al-Qulūb, and-went to house-of the-overseer, and-entered with his-wife; so-she-rose to-her and-kissed her-two-hands and-thanked her-kindness.
sentences.i: On the second day Qūt al-Qulūb mounted and went to the overseer's house and went in to his wife. The wife rose to meet her, kissed her hands and thanked her for her kindness.
sentences.n: ثاني يوم, “on the second day (i.e. the next)”, is the common idiom, here with فِي prefixed. Notice that دخلت عند زوجته uses عند, “at”, where Classical would use عَلَى; and that فقامت إليها has the overseer's wife as its subject, not Qūt al-Qulūb.

sentences.t: وَرَأَتْ أُمَّ غَانِمٍ وَأُخْتَهُ وَقَدَا دَخَلَتْهُمَا زَوْجَةُ الْعَرِيفِ الْحَمَّامَ وَغَيَّرَتْ مَا عَلَيْهِمَا مِنَ الثِّيَابِ فَظَهَرَتْ عَلَيْهِمَا آثَارُ النِّعْمَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-raʾat umma Ghānimin wa-ukhtahu wa-qadā dakhalat-humā zawjatu al-ʿarīfi al-ḥammāma wa-ghayyarat mā ʿalayhimā mina al-thiyābi fa-ẓaharat ʿalayhimā āthāru al-niʿmati
sentences.l: And-she-saw mother-of Ghānim and-his-sister, and-had made-enter-them-two the-wife-of the-overseer the-bath, and-changed what upon-the-two-of-them of the-clothes; so-appeared upon-the-two-of-them traces-of the-comfort.
sentences.i: And she saw Ghānim's mother and his sister, whom the overseer's wife had taken into the bath and changed out of their old clothes, so that the marks of comfort showed upon them.
sentences.n: The print has وقدا دخلتهما with the space misplaced; the letters are those of وقد أدخلتهما, “and had (she) made them enter”, and that is the sense. We keep the printed word division, so the first word carries the stray alif and the second the verb's remaining letters. The edition itself prints the hamza of ورأت and the madda of آثار.

sentences.t: فَجَلَسَتْ تُحَادِثُهُمَا سَاعَةً ثُمَّ سَأَلَتْ زَوْجَةَ الْعَرِيفِ عَنِ الْمَرِيضِ الَّذِي هُوَ عِنْدَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-jalasat tuḥādithuhumā sāʿatan thumma saʾalat zawjata al-ʿarīfi ʿani al-marīḍi alladhī huwa ʿindahā
sentences.l: So-she-sat conversing-with-them-two an-hour, then asked the-wife-of the-overseer about the-sick-one who he with-her.
sentences.i: She sat talking with them for an hour. Then she asked the overseer's wife about the sick man who was in her care.
sentences.n: سأل takes its person directly (زوجة العريف) and the matter with عَنْ, “about”; the answer comes in the next sentence.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ هُوَ بِحَالِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat huwa bi-ḥālihi
sentences.l: So-she-said: He in-his-state.
sentences.i: She said: He is just as he was.
sentences.n: بحاله, “in his state”, is the idiom for “unchanged”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ قُومُوا بِنَا نُطِلَّ عَلَيْهِ وَنَعُودَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat qūmū binā nuṭilla ʿalayhi wa-naʿūdahu
sentences.l: So-she-said: Rise with-us, we-look-in upon-him and-we-visit-him.
sentences.i: Then she said: Come, let us look in on him and visit him.
sentences.n: قوموا بنا is “rise with us”, i.e. “let us go”; the following subjunctives نطلّ ونعوده are the purpose clause, with no linking word. Classical تعالَوْا or a لِ would be expected; this is the Middle Arabic habit of simply juxtaposing the verbs.

sentences.t: فَقَامَتْ هِيَ وَزَوْجَةُ الْعَرِيفِ وَأُمُّ غَانِمٍ وَأُخْتُهُ وَدَخَلْنَ عَلَيْهِ وَجَلَسْنَ عِنْدَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāmat hiya wa-zawjatu al-ʿarīfi wa-ummu Ghānimin wa-ukhtuhu wa-dakhalna ʿalayhi wa-jalasna ʿindahu
sentences.l: So-rose she and-the-wife-of the-overseer and-mother-of Ghānim and-his-sister, and-they-entered upon-him and-sat with-him.
sentences.i: So she rose, with the overseer's wife and Ghānim's mother and sister, and they went in to him and sat beside him.
sentences.n: The verb قامت is singular, agreeing with the first subject, and the plural feminine دخلن / جلسن then takes over, as Classical practice allows.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَهُنَّ غَانِمُ بْنُ أَيُّوبَ الْمُتَيَّمُ الْمَسْلُوبُ يَذْكُرْنَ قُوتَ الْقُلُوبِ وَكَانَ قَدِ انْتَحَلَ جِسْمُهُ وَرَقَّ عَظْمُهُ رُدَّتْ لَهُ رُوحُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿahunna Ghānimu ibnu Ayyūba al-mutayyamu al-maslūbu yadhkurna Qūta al-Qulūbi wa-kāna qadi intaḥala jismuhu wa-raqqa ʿaẓmuhu ruddat lahu rūḥuhu
sentences.l: And-when heard-them Ghānim son-of Ayyūb, the-love-enslaved the-plundered, they-mentioning Qūt al-Qulūb, and-had wasted his-body and-grown-thin his-bone, was-returned to-him his-spirit.
sentences.i: When Ghānim son of Ayyūb, the lovesick one, the plundered one, heard the women speaking of Qūt al-Qulūb, though his body had wasted and his bones grown thin, his spirit came back to him.
sentences.n: المتيم المسلوب, “the love-enslaved, the despoiled”, is a rhyming pair of epithets for Ghānim. The verb يذكرن is a circumstantial clause, “as they were mentioning”. انتحل جسمه, “his body wasted away”, is the sense Lane gives for الانتحال of a body; the form is uncommon, but so printed. ردت له روحه is the stock phrase for revival; this unit is a main clause continued in the next.

sentences.t: وَشَالَ رَأْسَهُ مِنْ فَوْقِ الْمِخَدَّةِ وَنَادَى يَاقُوتَ الْقُلُوبِ
sentences.tr: wa-shāla raʾsahu min fawqi al-mikhaddati wa-nādā yā-Qūta al-Qulūbi
sentences.l: And-he-lifted his-head from above-of the-pillow and-called: O-Qūt al-Qulūb!
sentences.i: He lifted his head from the pillow and cried: O Qūt al-Qulūb!
sentences.n: شال, “lifted”, is a colloquial verb (Classical رَفَعَ); it recurs in Middle Arabic texts. يا قوت القلوب is printed as one word, يَاقُوتَ, the vocative يا joined to the name.

sentences.t: فَنَظَرَتْ إِلَيْهِ وَتَحَقَّقَتْهُ فَعَرَفَتْهُ وَصَاحَتْ
sentences.tr: fa-naẓarat ilayhi wa-taḥaqqaqat-hu fa-ʿarafat-hu wa-ṣāḥat
sentences.l: So-she-looked at-him and-made-sure-of-him and-knew-him and-cried-out.
sentences.i: She looked at him and studied him closely, and knew him, and cried out,
sentences.n: The sentence runs on: what she cried out follows in the next sentence.

sentences.t: بِقَوْلِهَا نَعَمْ يَاحَبِيبِي
sentences.tr: bi-qawlihā naʿam yā ḥabībī
sentences.l: With-her-saying: Yes, O-my-beloved.
sentences.i: with the words, “Yes, my darling.”
sentences.n: A continuation: بقولها (“by her saying”) hangs on the verb صاحت (“cried out”) just before. يا حبيبي is printed as one word (ياحبيبي), with no space after the vocative يا.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا اقْرَبِى مِنِّي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā iqrabī minnī
sentences.l: And-he-said to-her: Draw-near, you-(f.), from-me.
sentences.i: Then he said to her: Come closer to me.
sentences.n: اقربى is printed with a final ى (اقربي in a modern hand); we vocalise the feminine imperative as printed.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ لَعَلَّكَ غَانِمُ بْنُ أَيُّوبَ الْمُتَيَّمُ الْمَسْلُوبُ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu laʿallaka Ghānimu ibnu Ayyūba al-mutayyamu al-maslūbu
sentences.l: And-she-said to-him: Perhaps-you Ghānim son-of Ayyūb, the-love-enslaved, the-plundered.
sentences.i: And she said to him: Can you be Ghānim son of Ayyūb, the lovesick, the plundered?
sentences.n: لعلك here asks a tentative question (“can it be that you are…?”) rather than expressing hope. المتيم المسلوب, “the love-enslaved, the despoiled”, are the two epithets that cling to Ghānim in this tale; the sentence runs over from one printed line to the next.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا نَعَمْ أَنَا إِيَّاهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā naʿam anā iyyāhu
sentences.l: And-he-said to-her: Yes, I him.
sentences.i: Then he said to her: Yes, I am he.
sentences.n: أنا إياه, “I (am) him”, puts the object-form pronoun إياه where Classical Arabic would have أنا هو. This is a Middle Arabic usage; we vocalise what the text says.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ وَقَعَتْ مُغْشِيًّا عَلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika waqaʿat mughshiyyan ʿalayhā
sentences.l: And-at that, she-fell fainted-(m.) upon-her.
sentences.i: At that she fell down in a faint.
sentences.n: مغشيا عليها, “covered over, upon her”, is the fainting idiom. The participle stays masculine singular, as an unchanging adverbial; the next sentence has it again with dual subjects, so it is a set phrase here and not an agreement slip.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ أُخْتُهُ فِتْنَةُ وَأُمُّهُ كَلَامَهُمَا صَاحَتَا بِقَوْلِهِمَا وَافَرْحَتَاهُ وَوَقَعَتَا مُغْشِيًّا عَلَيْهِمَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿat ukhtuhu Fitnatu wa-ummuhu kalāmahumā ṣāḥatā bi-qawlihimā wā-farḥatāhu wa-waqaʿatā mughshiyyan ʿalayhimā
sentences.l: And-when heard his-sister Fitna and-his-mother the-speech-of-the-two-of-them, the-two-of-them-cried-out, with-their-saying: O-his-joy!, and-the-two-of-them-fell fainted upon-the-two-of-them.
sentences.i: When his sister Fitna and his mother heard what the two had said, they cried out, “Oh, what joy!”, and both fell down in a faint.
sentences.n: سمعت is singular though two people hear (the verb agrees with the nearer subject, أخته), then the dual returns in صاحتا. وافرحتاه is the cry of lamentation-form (nudba, wā-…-āh) turned to joy: “Oh, his gladness!” (or “Oh, our gladness!”). The dual ‘مغشيا’ again stays masculine singular. بقولهما: بـ here introduces the words they cried (“with their saying”).

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَ ذَلِكَ اسْتَفَاقَتَا فَقَالَتْ لَهُ قُوتُ الْقُلُوبِ
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda dhālika istafāqatā fa-qālat lahu Qūtu al-Qulūbi
sentences.l: And-after that, the-two-of-them-recovered, and-said to-him Qūt al-Qulūb:
sentences.i: After that the two women came to, and Qūt al-Qulūb said to him:

sentences.t: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي جَمَعَ شَمْلَنَا بِكَ وَبِأُمِّكَ وَأُخْتِكَ
sentences.tr: al-ḥamdu li-llāhi alladhī jamaʿa shamlanā bika wa-bi-ummika wa-ukhtika
sentences.l: The-praise to-God who gathered our-union through-you and-through-your-mother and-your-sister.
sentences.i: Praise be to God, who has brought us together again through you, your mother and your sister.
sentences.n: شمل is the “gathered whole” of a family; جمع شملنا is the stock phrase for reunion. بك here means “by means of you”, with the بـ repeated before the second person (وبأمك) but not the third (واختك), which rides on it.

sentences.t: فَتَقَدَّمَتْ إِلَيْهِ وَحَكَتْ لَهُ عَلَى جَمِيعِ مَاجَرَى لَهَا مَعَ الْخَلِيفَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-taqaddamat ilayhi wa-ḥakat lahu ʿalā jamīʿi mā jarā lahā maʿa al-khalīfati
sentences.l: And-she-advanced to-him and-related to-him upon all-of what happened to-her with the-caliph,
sentences.i: Then she came forward to him and told him everything that had happened to her with the caliph,
sentences.n: حكى على, “relate upon”, is not Classical (which says حكى له ما جرى or حكى عن); we vocalise as printed. The sentence continues in the next unit.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ لَهُ إِنِّي أَظْهَرْتُ لِأَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ الْحَقَّ فَصَدَّقَ كَلَامِي وَرَضِيَ عَنْكَ
sentences.tr: wa-qālat lahu innī aẓhartu li-amīri al-muʾminīna al-ḥaqqa fa-ṣaddaqa kalāmī wa-raḍiya ʿanka
sentences.l: And-she-said to-him: Indeed-I I-showed to-the-Commander-of the-believers the-truth, so-he-believed my-speech and-was-pleased with-you.
sentences.i: and she told him: I made the truth plain to the Commander of the Faithful; he believed my words and is pleased with you.
sentences.n: لِـ in لأمير means “to”: she showed the truth to the caliph. رضي عنك, “was satisfied away from you”, is the idiom for being pleased with someone (رضي عن).

sentences.t: وَهُوَ الْيَوْمَ يَتَمَنَّى أَنْ يَرَاكَ
sentences.tr: wa-huwa al-yawma yatamannā an yarāka
sentences.l: And-he today wishes that he-sees-you.
sentences.i: Today he longs to see you.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهَا أَخْبَرَتْهُ أَنَّهُ وَهَبَنِي لَكَ
sentences.tr: thumma innahā akhbaratuhu annahu wahabanī laka
sentences.l: Then indeed-she informed-him that-he gave-me to-you.
sentences.i: Then she told him that the caliph had given her to him.
sentences.n: The text slips from reported speech into the speaker's own voice: وهبني is “gave me”, where the reported form would be وهبها, “gave her”. Rather than regularise it, the idiomatic line gives the sense. لك: لِـ marks the person given to (“to you”).

sentences.t: فَفَرِحَ بِذَلِكَ غَايَةَ الْفَرَحِ
sentences.tr: fa-fariḥa bi-dhālika ghāyata al-faraḥi
sentences.l: And-he-rejoiced at-that, the-extreme-of the-joy.
sentences.i: He rejoiced at this beyond measure.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُمْ قُوتُ الْقُلُوبِ لَاتَبْرَحُوا حَتَّى أَحْضُرَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahum Qūtu al-Qulūbi lā tabraḥū ḥattā aḥḍura
sentences.l: And-said to-them Qūt al-Qulūb: Not depart until I-come!
sentences.i: Then Qūt al-Qulūb said to them: Do not leave until I come back.
sentences.n: We read أحضر as aḥḍura, “I come (am present)”, which suits her going away and returning; أُحْضِرَ, “I bring”, is the other possible pointing, but no object is given. لا تبرحوا is printed joined as one word.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهَا قَامَتْ مِنْ وَقْتِهَا وَسَاعَتِهَا وَانْطَلَقَتْ إِلَى قَصْرِهَا
sentences.tr: thumma innahā qāmat min waqtihā wa-sāʿatihā wa-inṭalaqat ilā qaṣrihā
sentences.l: Then indeed-she rose from her-time and-her-hour, and-set-off to her-palace,
sentences.i: Then she got up that very moment and hurried to her palace,
sentences.n: من وقتها وساعتها, “from her time and her hour”, is the stock phrase for “at once”; the two nearly synonymous nouns are doubled for emphasis.

sentences.t: وَحَمَلَتِ الصُّنْدُوقَ الَّذِي أَخَذَتْهُ مِنْ دَارِهِ وَأَخْرَجَتْ مِنْهُ دَنَانِيرَ
sentences.tr: wa-ḥamalati al-ṣundūqa alladhī akhadhathu min dārihi wa-akhrajat minhu danānīra
sentences.l: and-took-up the-chest which she-took from his-house, and-brought-out from-it dinars,
sentences.i: took up the chest she had taken from his house, and drew some dinars out of it,
sentences.n: The chest is the one she took from Ghānim's house earlier in the tale. The sentence continues from the previous unit.

sentences.t: وَأَعْطَتْ لِلْعَرِيفِ إِيَّاهَا
sentences.tr: wa-aʿṭat li-al-ʿarīfi iyyāhā
sentences.l: and-gave to-the-overseer them.
sentences.i: and gave them to the overseer.
sentences.n: أعطى لِـ for “give to” (Classical simply takes two objects) and the detached إياها, “them”, are Middle Arabic touches.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ لَهُ خُذْ هَذِهِ الدَّرَاهِمَ وَاشْتَرِ لِكُلِّ شَخْصٍ مِنْهُمْ أَرْبَعَ بَدَلَاتٍ كَوَامِلَ مِنْ أَحْسَنِ الْقُمَاشِ وَعِشْرِينَ مِنْدِيلًا وَغَيْرَ ذَلِكَ مِمَّا يَحْتَاجُونَ إِلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: wa-qālat lahu khudh hādhihi al-darāhima wa-ishtari li-kulli shakhṣin minhum arbaʿa badalātin kawāmila min aḥsani al-qumāshi wa-ʿishrīna mindīlan wa-ghayra dhālika mimmā yaḥtājūna ilayhi
sentences.l: And-she-said to-him: Take these the-dirhams, and-buy for-every person of-them four suits complete, of best-of the-cloth, and-twenty handkerchief, and-other-than that, of-what they-need to-it.
sentences.i: and said to him: Take these dirhams and buy for each of them four complete suits of the finest cloth, twenty handkerchiefs, and whatever else they need.
sentences.n: She hands over dinars but calls them الدراهم, “dirhams”: the text uses the two coins loosely, and we keep its word. بدلات are suits of clothes; مما يحتاجون إليه, “of what they need to it”, repeats the preposition that يحتاج takes (احتاج إلى). عشرين منديلا keeps the singular noun after “twenty”, as Classical Arabic requires.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهَا دَخَلَتْ بِهِمَا وَبِغَانِمٍ الْحَمَّامَ وَأَمَرَتْ بِغَسْلِهِمْ
sentences.tr: thumma innahā dakhalat bihimā wa-bi-Ghānimin al-ḥammāma wa-amarat bi-ghaslihim
sentences.l: Then indeed-she entered with-the-two-of-them and-with-Ghānim the-bath, and-ordered the-washing-of-them.
sentences.i: Then she took the two women and Ghānim into the bathhouse and ordered them to be washed.
sentences.n: دخل بـ is “enter with”, that is, take someone in with oneself; أمر بغسلهم uses بـ because أمر takes it for the thing commanded.

sentences.t: وَعَمِلَتْ لَهُمُ الْمَسَالِيقَ وَمَاءَ الْخُولَنْجَانِ وَمَاءَ التُّفَّاحِ بَعْدَأَنْ خَرَجُوا مِنَ الْحَمَّامِ وَلَبِسُوا الثِّيَابَ
sentences.tr: wa-ʿamilat lahumu al-masālīqa wa-māʾa al-khūlanjāni wa-māʾa al-tuffāḥi baʿdaʾan kharajū mina al-ḥammāmi wa-labisū al-thiyāba
sentences.l: And-she-made for-them the-boiled-meats, and-water-of the-galangal and-water-of the-apples, after-that they-came-out from the-bath and-wore the-clothes.
sentences.i: She prepared for them broths of boiled meat, galangal water and apple water, once they had come out of the bath and put on their clothes.
sentences.n: بعدأن is بعد أن, “after that”, printed as one word; the hamza of أن is ours. المساليق are boiled meats or broths; الخولنجان is galangal (a medicinal root), here drunk as a restorative.

sentences.t: وَأَقَامَتْ عِنْدَهُمْ ثَلٰثَةَ أَيَّامٍ وَهِيَ تُطْعِمُهُمْ لَحْمَ الدَّجَاجِ وَالْمَسَالِيقَ وَتَسْقِيهِمُ السُّكَّرَ الْمُكَرَّرَ
sentences.tr: wa-aqāmat ʿindahum thalāthata ayyāmin wa-hiya tuṭʿimuhum laḥma al-dajāji wa-al-masālīqa wa-tasqīhimu al-sukkara al-mukarrara
sentences.l: And-she-stayed with-them three days, and-she feeding-them flesh-of the-fowl and-the-boiled-meats and-giving-them-to-drink the-sugar the-refined.
sentences.i: She stayed with them three days, feeding them chicken and broths and giving them refined sugar to drink.
sentences.n: ثلثة is printed without the alif; the dagger alif on the lām restores ثَلاثة. The clause وهي تطعمهم is a circumstantial ḥāl clause: “while she was feeding them”.

sentences.t: فَبَعْدَ ثَلٰثَةِ أَيَّامٍ رُدَّتْ أَرْوَاحُهُمْ لَهُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-baʿda thalāthati ayyāmin ruddat arwāḥuhum lahum
sentences.l: So-after three-of days were-returned their-spirits to-them.
sentences.i: After three days their spirits were restored to them.
sentences.n: “Their spirits were returned to them” is the idiom for recovering strength and courage after hardship.

sentences.t: فَأَدْخَلَتْهُمُ الْحَمَّامَ ثَانِيًا وَخَرَجُوا وَغَيَّرَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ الثِّيَابَ وَخَلَّتْهُمْ فِي بَيْتِ الْعَرِيفِ
sentences.tr: fa-adkhalat-humu al-ḥammāma thāniyan wa-kharajū wa-ghayyarat ʿalayhimu al-thiyāba wa-khallat-hum fī bayti al-ʿarīfi
sentences.l: So-she-made-enter-them the-bath a-second-time, and-they-came-out, and-she-changed upon-them the-clothes, and-left-them in house-of the-overseer.
sentences.i: Then she took them into the bath a second time, and they came out, and she changed their clothes, and she left them in the house of the overseer.
sentences.n: وخلتهم is printed without a shadda; we read it as خَلَّتْهُمْ, “she left them” (خَلَّى), which suits the sense. العريف is the overseer, the headman of a quarter or of the household.

sentences.t: وَذَهَبَتْ إِلَى الْقَصْرِ فَاسْتَأْذَنَتِ الْخَلِيفَةَ فَأَذِنَ لَهَا
sentences.tr: wa-dhahabat ilā al-qaṣri fa-staʾdhanati al-khalīfata fa-adhina lahā
sentences.l: And-she-went to the-palace, and-asked-leave-of the-caliph, and-he-permitted to-her.
sentences.i: She went to the palace and asked the caliph for leave to enter, and he gave it.

sentences.t: فَدَخَلَتْ وَقَبَّلَتِ الْأَرْضَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَأَعْلَمَتْهُ بِالْقِصَّةِ
sentences.tr: fa-dakhalat wa-qabbalati al-arḍa bayna yadayhi wa-aʿlamat-hu bi-al-qiṣṣati
sentences.l: So-she-entered and-kissed the-ground between his-two-hands, and-informed-him of-the-story.
sentences.i: She went in, kissed the ground before him, and told him the whole story.
sentences.n: بين يديه, “between his two hands”, means “in his presence”.

sentences.t: وَأَنَّهُ قَدْ حَضَرَ سَيِّدُهَا غَانِمُ بْنُ أَيُّوبَ الْمُتَيَّمُ الْمَسْلُوبُ وَأَنَّ أُمَّهُ وَأُخْتَهُ قَدْ حَضَرَتَا
sentences.tr: wa-annahu qad ḥaḍara sayyiduhā Ghānimu ibnu Ayyūba al-mutayyamu al-maslūbu wa-anna ummahu wa-ukhtahu qad ḥaḍaratā
sentences.l: And-that-he has arrived her-master Ghānim son-of Ayyūb, the-love-enslaved, the-plundered, and-that his-mother and-his-sister have arrived-(dual).
sentences.i: She told him that her master Ghānim son of Ayyūb, the lovesick, the plundered, had arrived, and that his mother and his sister had arrived as well.
sentences.n: A continuation of the previous sentence: the two clauses with أنّ depend on أعلمته, “she informed him”. Note the dual حضرتا for the two women. In the print the epithets المتيم المسلوب read as nominatives; we point them so, in apposition to غانم. المتيم is one enslaved by love; المسلوب one stripped of his goods.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْخَلِيفَةُ كَلَامَ قُوتِ الْقُلُوبِ قَالَ لِلْخُدَّامِ عَلَيَّ بِغَانِمٍ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-khalīfatu kalāma Qūti al-Qulūbi qāla li-al-khuddāmi ʿalayya bi-Ghānimin
sentences.l: And-when heard the-caliph speech-of Qūt al-Qulūb, he-said to-the-servants: Upon-me with-Ghānim!
sentences.i: When the caliph heard what Qūt al-Qulūb said, he told the attendants: Bring me Ghānim!
sentences.n: عليّ بـ followed by a name is a stock command: “[bring] to me …!”, with the verb left unsaid. The direct speech has no introducing particle.

sentences.t: فَنَزَلَ جَعْفَرٌ إِلَيْهِ وَكَانَتْ قَدْ سَبَقَتْهُ قُوتُ الْقُلُوبِ وَدَخَلَتْ عَلَى غَانِمٍ وَأَعْلَمَتْهُ أَنَّ الْخَلِيفَةَ أَرْسَلَ إِلَيْكَ يَطْلُبُكَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-nazala Jaʿfarun ilayhi wa-kānat qad sabaqat-hu Qūtu al-Qulūbi wa-dakhalat ʿalā Ghānimin wa-aʿlamat-hu anna al-khalīfata arsala ilayka yaṭlubuka bayna yadayhi
sentences.l: So-went-down Jaʿfar to-him; and-had she-preceded-him Qūt al-Qulūb, and-entered upon Ghānim and-informed-him that the-caliph has-sent to-you, seeking-you between his-two-hands.
sentences.i: Jaʿfar went down to fetch him; but Qūt al-Qulūb had gone ahead of him, and had come in to Ghānim and told him that the caliph had sent for him and wanted him in his presence.
sentences.n: The verb كانت precedes its feminine subject قوت القلوب, as is regular. “Had gone ahead” is built from كان + قد + the perfect.

sentences.t: فَأَوْصَتْهُ بِفَصَاحَةِ لِسَانِهِ وَتَثْبِيتِ جَنَانِهِ وَعُذُوبَةِ كَلَامِهِ وَأَلْبَسَتْهُ حُلَّةً فَاخِرَةً وَأَعْطَتْهُ دَنَانِيرَ بِكَثْرَةٍ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-awṣat-hu bi-faṣāḥati lisānihi wa-tathbīti janānihi wa-ʿudhūbati kalāmihi wa-albasat-hu ḥullatan fākhiratan wa-aʿṭat-hu danānīra bi-kathratin wa-qālat lahu
sentences.l: So-she-charged-him with-eloquence-of his-tongue and-steadying-of his-heart and-sweetness-of his-speech, and-clothed-him a-robe splendid, and-gave-him dinars in-abundance, and-said to-him:
sentences.i: She charged him to speak eloquently, to keep a steady heart and a sweet tongue; she dressed him in a splendid robe, gave him dinars in plenty, and said to him:
sentences.n: أوصاه بـ, “charge someone with”, takes the thing urged with بِـ. The three genitives, لسانه / جنانه / كلامه, rhyme (sajʿ) in -ānihi / -āmihi. The speech she makes follows in the next unit.

sentences.t: كَثِّرِ الْبَذْلَ إِلَى حَاشِيَةِ الْخَلِيفَةِ وَأَنْتَ دَاخِلٌ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: kaththiri al-badhla ilā ḥāshiyati al-khalīfati wa-anta dākhilun ʿalayhi
sentences.l: Multiply the-giving to retinue-of the-caliph, and-you entering upon-him.
sentences.i: Give lavishly to the caliph's retinue as you go in to him.
sentences.n: وأنت داخل عليه is a circumstantial clause, “while you are going in to him”; the quotation ends after عليه, and the following وإذا ب- resumes the narrative. حاشية is the retinue or entourage.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا بِجَعْفَرٍ قَدْ أَقْبَلَ عَلَيْهِ وَهُوَ عَلَى بَغْلَتِهِ النُّوبِيَّةِ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā bi-Jaʿfarin qad aqbala ʿalayhi wa-huwa ʿalā baghlatihi al-nūbiyyati
sentences.l: And-behold, with-Jaʿfar, he-has advanced upon-him, and-he upon his-mule the-Nubian.
sentences.i: And suddenly Jaʿfar came toward him, riding his Nubian mule.
sentences.n: وإذا بـ marks sudden appearance: “and behold, Jaʿfar!”; the بِـ adds no meaning of its own. The Nubian mule is a prized mount.

sentences.t: فَقَامَ غَانِمٌ وَقَابَلَهُ وَحَيَّاهُ وَبَاسَ الْأَرْضَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَقَدْ ظَهَرَ كَوْكَبُ سَعْدِهِ وَأَضَاءَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāma Ghānimun wa-qābalahu wa-ḥayyāhu wa-bāsa al-arḍa bayna yadayhi wa-qad ẓahara kawkabu saʿdihi wa-aḍāʾa
sentences.l: So-rose Ghānim and-met-him and-greeted-him and-kissed the-ground between his-two-hands, and-had appeared the-star-of his-felicity and-shone.
sentences.i: Ghānim rose, met him, greeted him, and kissed the ground before him, for the star of his good fortune had risen and shone.
sentences.n: باس, “he kissed”, is a colloquial-leaning verb for the Classical قَبَّلَ (as in the previous sentences). The final وقد clause is circumstantial: his luck had turned.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَهُ جَعْفَرٌ وَمَازَالَا سَائِرِينَ هُوَ وَجَعْفَرٌ حَتَّى دَخَلَا عَلَى أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadha-hu Jaʿfarun wa-mā zālā sāʾirīna huwa wa-Jaʿfarun ḥattā dakhalā ʿalā amīri al-muʾminīna
sentences.l: So-took-him Jaʿfar, and-not ceased-(dual) going, he and-Jaʿfar, until entered-(dual) upon commander-of the-believers.
sentences.i: Jaʿfar took him along, and the two of them walked on together until they went in to the Commander of the Faithful.
sentences.n: ما زالا سائرين, “they did not cease going”, is the regular way to say “they kept on going”. In هو وجعفر the dual verb is followed by the two named subjects.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا حَضَرَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ḥaḍara bayna yadayhi
sentences.l: And-when he-was-present between his-two-hands,
sentences.i: When he stood before him,
sentences.n: A fragment: the main clause follows in the next sentence.

sentences.t: نَظَرَ إِلَى الْوُزَرَاءِ وَالْأُمَرَاءِ وَالْحُجَّابِ وَالنُّوَّابِ وَأَرْبَابِ الدَّوْلَةِ وَأَصْحَابِ الصَّوْلَةِ
sentences.tr: naẓara ilā al-wuzarāʾi wa-al-umarāʾi wa-al-ḥujjābi wa-al-nuwwābi wa-arbābi al-dawlati wa-aṣḥābi al-ṣawlati
sentences.l: Looked to the-viziers and-the-emirs and-the-chamberlains and-the-deputies and-lords-of the-state and-possessors-of the-might.
sentences.i: He looked at the viziers and emirs, the chamberlains and deputies, the lords of the state and the men of might.
sentences.n: The main clause of the sentence begun just before; its subject, “he”, is Ghānim, who is about to address the caliph. Four titles in a row, then the rhyming close أرباب الدولة / أصحاب الصولة, “lords of the state / masters of might”.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ غَانِمٌ أَعْذَبَ كَلَامَهُ وَفَصَاحَتَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika Ghānimun aʿdhaba kalāmahu wa-faṣāḥatahu
sentences.l: And-at that, Ghānim made-sweet his-speech and-his-eloquence.
sentences.i: Thereupon Ghānim sweetened his speech and his eloquence to the utmost.
sentences.n: The verb أعذب is unusual in this sense; I take it as the form IV “made sweet, used the sweetest of”. Another possible reading is the elative أَعْذَبُ, “sweetest (of) his speech”, with غانم left hanging, but the accusative reading gives the smoother sentence. The sentence also places the subject before its verb, as often in this text.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ نَظَرَ إِلَى الْخَلِيفَةِ وَأَطْرَقَ بِرَأْسِهِ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ وَأَنْشَدَ يَقُولُ هَذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتَ
sentences.tr: thumma naẓara ilā al-khalīfati wa-aṭraqa bi-raʾsihi ilā al-arḍi wa-anshada yaqūlu hādhihi al-abyāta
sentences.l: Then he-looked to the-caliph, and-bowed with-his-head to the-earth, and-recited, saying these the-verses.
sentences.i: Then he looked toward the caliph, bowed his head to the ground, and recited these verses.
sentences.n: أطرق برأسه, “he lowered with his head”, is the idiom for bowing the head; the بِـ is the usual one after أطرق. يقول after أنشد is a redundant “saying”, a common Nights habit for introducing verse.

sentences.t:
حُبِيتَ مِنْ مَلِكٍ عَظِيمِ الشَّانِ * مُتَتَابِعِ الْحَسَنَاتِ وَالْاِحْسَانِ
لَا يُلْهَجُونَ بِغَيْرِهِ مِنْ قَيْصَرٍ * فِي ذَاالْمَقَامِ وَصَاحِبِ الْاِيوَانِ
تَضَعُ الْمُلُوكُ عَلَى ثَرَى اَعْتَابِهِ * عِنْدَالسَّلَامِ جَوَاهِرُ التِّيجَانِ
حَتَّى اِذَا بَصُرَتْ لَهُ اَبْصَارُهُمْ * خَرُّوا لِهَيْبَتِهِ عَلَى الْاَذْقَانِ
sentences.tr:
ḥubīta min malikin ʿaẓīmi al-shāni * mutatābiʿi al-ḥasanāti wa-al-iḥsāni
lā yulhajūna bi-ghayrihi min qayṣarin * fī dhā al-maqāmi wa-ṣāḥibi al-īwāni
taḍaʿu al-mulūku ʿalā tharā aʿtābihi * ʿinda al-salāmi jawāhiru al-tījāni
ḥattā idhā baṣurat lahu abṣāruhum * kharrū li-haybatihi ʿalā al-adhqāni
sentences.l:
You-were-favoured from a-king great-of the-standing * successive-of the-good-deeds and-the-beneficence.
Not they-are-made-devoted with-other-than-him, of Caesar * in this the-station, and-lord-of the-Īwān.
Lay the-kings upon dust-of his-thresholds * at the-salutation, jewels-of the-crowns,
until when looked-keenly for-him their-eyes * they-fell for-his-awe upon the-chins.
sentences.i:
You are favoured by a king of mighty standing, who gives good deed after good deed and kindness after kindness.
None cling to any but him, not Caesar in his high place, nor the lord of the Īwān.
Kings lay the jewels of their crowns on the dust of his thresholds when they salute him,
until, when their eyes light upon him, they fall on their chins in awe of him.
sentences.n: The print gives pointing to this poem, and it is kept exactly as printed, so a few vowels are the edition's own and not what strict grammar would give. In the second line يلهجون, “they are made devoted”, is a passive of unclear sense; the line seems to say that all rulers, even Caesar and the Persian king (“lord of the Īwān”), are loyal to no one else. In the third line الملوك and جواهر are both nominative as printed, which does not fit تضع, “lays”; read the kings as laying the jewels of their crowns, and treat the nominative ending on جواهر as a slip. In the fourth line, to fall on the chins (الأذقان) is the Qurʾanic posture of prostration.

sentences.t:
وَيُفِيدُهُمْ ذَالَ الْمَقَامُ مَعَ الرِّضَى * رُتَبَ الْعُلَا وَجَلَالَةَ السُّلْطَانِ
ضَاقَتْ بِعَسْكَرِكَ الْفَيَافِي وَالْوَرَى * فَاضْرِبْ خِيَامَكَ فِي ذُرَى كِيْوَانِ
اَبْقَاكَ مَا لِيكَ الْمُلُوكِ بِعَنْوَةٍ * لَكَ حُسْنُ تَدْبِيرٍ وَثَبْتُ جِنَانِ
وَنَشَرْتَ عَدْلَكَ فِي الْبَسِيطَةِ كُلِّهَا * حَتَّى اسْتَوَى الْقَاصِي بِهَا وَالدَّانِي
sentences.tr:
wa-yufīduhum dhāla al-maqāmu maʿa al-ridā * rutaba al-ʿulā wa-jalālata al-sulṭāni
ḍāqat bi-ʿaskarika al-fayāfī wa-al-warā * fa-iḍrib khiyāmaka fī dhurā Kaywāni
abqāka mā līka al-mulūki bi-ʿanwatin * laka ḥusnu tadbīrin wa-thabtu jināni
wa-nasharta ʿadlaka fī al-basīṭati kullihā * ḥattā istawā al-qāṣī bihā wa-al-dānī
sentences.l:
And-benefits-them that the-station with the-favour * ranks-of the-eminence and-majesty-of the-sultanate.
Grew-narrow with-your-army the-wastelands and-the-creation * so strike your-tents in peaks-of Saturn.
May-keep-you Lord(?)-of the-kings, by-force; * yours good-of management and-steadiness-of heart.
And-you-spread your-justice in the-earth all-of-it * until became-equal the-far in-it and-the-near.
sentences.i:
That high station, together with favour, bestows on them ranks of eminence and the majesty of sovereignty.
The deserts and all creation grow too narrow for your army, so pitch your tents on the heights of Saturn.
May the Lord of kings preserve you; yours are sound judgement and a steady heart.
You have spread your justice through the whole wide earth, until the far and the near in it stand equal.
sentences.n: Verse as printed, with the edition's own pointing. In the first line ذال is printed for ذلك, “that”; take it as a slip or a clipped form. The third line is the roughest: ما ليك الملوك is printed as two words, and the likeliest sense is مالك الملوك, “Master of kings”, a title of God; بعنوة, “by force, by submission”, is obscure in this place and I give it as printed. كيوان is Saturn, the highest planet in the old scheme, so “the heights of Saturn” means the very top of the sky.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ مِنْ شِعْرِهِ طَرِبَ الْخَلِيفَةُ وَأَعْجَبَهُ فَصَاحَةُ لِسَانِهِ وَعُذُوبَةُ مَنْطِقِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faragha min shiʿrihi ṭariba al-khalīfatu wa-aʿjabahu faṣāḥatu lisānihi wa-ʿudhūbatu manṭiqihi
sentences.l: And-when he-finished from his-poetry, was-moved-with-delight the-caliph, and-pleased-him eloquence-of his-tongue and-sweetness-of his-speech.
sentences.i: When he had finished his poem, the caliph was moved to delight, and he was charmed by the eloquence of his tongue and the sweetness of his speech.
sentences.n: The two nouns after أعجبه are the subjects of a singular verb, which is regular when the verb comes first.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَ زَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahra Zāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And-overtook Shahrazād the-morning, and-she-fell-silent from the-speech the-permitted.
sentences.i: And morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech.
sentences.n: The closing formula, in rhyme: الصباح / المباح. The print writes the name as two words, شهر زاد; it is the same Shahrazād. Here the night ends, in the middle of the tale.
